name: @clossys/writer

capabilities.subQuestion: Is the voice record itself complete — every field bound, every rule derived from a real brand attribute?
capabilities.worldClass: The voice record is fully bound (no unedited template placeholder) and every rule traces to a brand-derivation attribute — checked as a record, before any copy is ever measured against it.

capabilities.subQuestion: Is every registry entry itself schema-valid, unique, and free of unfilled placeholders?
capabilities.worldClass: Every registry entry is schema-valid, has a unique id, and every declared placeholder is present in its own text — registry validity only; whether a component actually USES the registry by id is addressability's own question.

capabilities.subQuestion: Does every user-facing string in code trace to a registered copy entry, by literal match or citation?
capabilities.worldClass: Every component string either matches a registered CopyRecord entry's text/alias or carries a copy:<id> citation -- the "approved copy coverage rate" metric this role owns (docs/contracts/role-loop-archetypes.json), and what writer-check's default command (copy-clean) actually proves. Distinct from `copy-registry` (is the registry entry itself valid) and from `claims-to-copy-traceability` (does a claim-SHAPED sentence cite an approved Strategist claim).

capabilities.subQuestion: Does every claim-shaped or numeric sentence in shipped copy trace to an approved registry claim, by citation?
capabilities.worldClass: A currency amount, percentage, multiplier, or superlative sentence in live copy either matches a registered claim's text or carries a claim:<id> citation to one -- checked on the COPY side. Whether Strategist's own facts/markers gate should stop scanning shipped surfaces at all (leaving this the one place that check happens) is a decision pending #1271, not yet a settled boundary -- today `strategist-check` still scans authored prose too (its own facts-clean fixture is an announcement.md).

capabilities.subQuestion: Does live, shipped copy still match its registry source and stay within its word-budget and fold rules?
capabilities.worldClass: Shipped copy never drifts silently from its registry source, and the above-the-fold word budget is enforced, not eyeballed.

capabilities.subQuestion: Is every piece of user-facing prose resolved from the registry by id, never typed directly into a component?
capabilities.worldClass: A rename is always cheap: renaming a piece of copy means editing one registry entry, never hunting every component that typed the sentence — #1208's site template reads copy by id on this guarantee.

capabilities.subQuestion: Does the whole set of a project's locales actually cover the same ground, current and correctly interpolating?
capabilities.worldClass: Every target locale covers what the source locale covers, with no orphaned or stale translation — governance over WHICH locales are covered, not runtime translation itself.

capabilities.subQuestion: Is shipped copy actually well said — in voice, in tense, in person, every claim supported?
capabilities.worldClass: Every mechanically detectable voice violation (forbidden term, wrong tense or person, an unsupported claim marked as requiring support) is caught against the bound voice record — the answer to "is it well said", not merely "does it trace".

capabilities.subQuestion: Does the product have one governed tagline, pitch-length set, boilerplate, and FAQ that everything else derives from?
capabilities.worldClass: One governed messaging kit (tagline, short/medium/long pitch, short/medium/long boilerplate, FAQ) exists and every surface's short-form copy derives from it, per #1204's Identity layer, rather than being improvised per surface.

description: The writer role: is it well said? A consumer-owned language system: voice rules, glossary and claims validation, addressable copy records, source traceability, locale coverage, and passage-layer composition — five gates reachable from one bin. Ships machinery and templates, never a consumer's actual copy or voice.
author: Clossys
